title: Surgical Removal of Sea Cucumber Gonads
author: Jon Eilers
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5pag5ie

steps.title: Anesthetize the Sea Cucumber
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the sea cucumber following the specific protocol at dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5nyg5fw.

steps.title: Locate Gonadopore and Prepare Skin
steps.instruction: Locate the gonadopore just posterior to the head of the sea cucumber and pinch the skin immediately behind it.

steps.title: Create Body Wall Incision
steps.instruction: Create a small incision in the body wall to access the gonads.

substeps.instruction: Push the pointed side of the dissection scissors into the body wall approximately one centimeter posterior to the gonadopore until the blade pierces the wall.
Angle the scissors towards the back of the sea cucumber and cut a one to two centimeter incision.
Remove the scissors from the incision.

steps.title: Extract Gonads
steps.instruction: Remove the gonads from the body cavity and manage any expelled internal organs.

substeps.instruction: Allow body cavity pressure to push the gonads and fluid out of the incision.
Remove the gonads and place them into falcon tubes on ice.
Use a spatula to push any expelled internal organs (such as the respiratory tree or intestines) back into the sea cucumber to prevent evisceration.

steps.title: Suture the Wound
steps.instruction: Close the incision using standard medical stitching techniques.

substeps.instruction: Use suture, forceps, and hemostat forceps to stitch the wound closed.

steps.title: Post-Operative Care and Stitch Removal
steps.instruction: Return the animal to its container and monitor for healing.

substeps.instruction: Place the sea cucumber back in its container.
Allow the wound to heal for 2-3 days.
Cut and remove the stitches once healed to prevent lesion formation.
